Mutations in GANAB and PRKCSH disrupt the ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and subsequent cyst formation in the kidneys and liver.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in GANAB or PRKCSH in individuals diagnosed with either polycystic kidney disease 3 or polycystic liver disease 1, or identification of distinct molecular pathways affected by mutations in each disease independently. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the ERAD pathway in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting protein folding and degradation for treating both conditions.

Similarly, mutations in MOGS also impair N-linked glycosylation, causing MOGS-congenital disorder of glycosylation. The convergence is on the shared pathway of N-linked glycosylation, affecting protein maturation and cellular function in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in GANAB or MOGS were found to have completely independent downstream effects on cellular processes, not converging on any shared aspect of protein glycosylation or related cellular machinery, this hypothesis would be falsified. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of N-linked glycosylation in both PKD3 and MOGS-CDG could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream pathways or protein maturation processes, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
